title: Ambani’s Jio set to open India’s biggest IPO from Oct 21, valued at nearly $108Bn
key_facts: Jio Platforms opens bidding for India's largest IPO on 21 Oct, per a company filing; subscription closes 23 Oct and trading is expected 28 Oct.
Price band is ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 per share; at the top it raises about $3.2 billion and values the company at roughly $108 billion.
This would top Hyundai Motor India's 2024 offering.
The valuation is lower than earlier talk of $130 to $170 billion.
270 million new shares are offered, mostly to repay debt; Meta and Google are not selling.
Bloomberg reports the anchor book alone may draw bids above $20 billion.
Reliance Jio Infocomm has 524 million subscribers and about 60% of India's data traffic.
quote_evidence: Jio Platforms will open bidding for what’s set to be India’s largest-ever initial public offering on October 21, according to a company filing.
Meta and Google, which count among Jio’s major foreign investors, aren’t selling into this offering.
why_it_matters_hint: India's biggest-ever listing, in a company that connects half a billion people.
notes: Article mixes reporting and opinion ('humble rather than heroic'); opinion left out.
